prompt: Do you have any questions for us?
variants: What would you like to know about the role or the team?
Anything you want to ask before we finish?
intent: Shows preparation and genuine interest; a candidate with no questions looks passive.
answerGuide: Ask: What does a successful first 90 days look like in this role?
Ask: What are the biggest challenges the team is facing right now?
Ask: How does the team work day to day (tools, rhythm, how work is handed over)?
Prepare four and ask the two or three still unanswered.
pitfalls: Asking about pay or perks first.
followUps: What is most important to you in the answer?
Does that change your view of the role?

prompt: What questions would you ask a hiring manager about the team and how success is measured?
variants: Questions about the role to ask the hiring manager.
intent: Quality of the questions reveals how you think about the job.
answerGuide: How will my performance be measured and reviewed?
What would you want someone in this role to have accomplished by six months?
What does the team do well, and where do you want to improve?
Who will I work with most closely?
followUps: What would you do with the answer?

prompt: What questions would you ask in a recruiter phone screen?
variants: What should I ask the recruiter?
intent: Practical, logistics-focused questions suit the first call.
answerGuide: What are the next steps and timeline?
Is the role fully remote, and are there core hours or time-zone expectations?
What is the team structure and who would I report to?
What does the interview process involve?
pitfalls: Asking for detailed technical info the recruiter lacks.
followUps: Is there a range for this role?

prompt: Questions to ask about remote work and collaboration at this company.
variants: What would you ask about remote culture?
intent: Shows that you have thought about the practicalities of remote collaboration and want to confirm how this team handles them.
answerGuide: How does the team communicate day to day, and how much is asynchronous?
How are decisions and documentation shared across the team?
How do remote employees get feedback and growth opportunities?
Are there regular meetings, and what are the core hours?
pitfalls: Asking if you can work whenever you like.
followUps: What would help you do well remotely?

prompt: Questions to ask about the tools, process and quality of the work.
variants: What would you ask a QA or product lead?
intent: Signals craft interest for QA, BA and product roles.
answerGuide: What tools does the team use for tickets, testing and documentation?
How do you handle release testing and who signs off?
What does the backlog process look like and who decides priority?
What is a recent thing the team improved?

prompt: Questions to ask about customers, onboarding and support.
variants: What would you ask a customer success or support manager?
intent: Shows customer orientation through questions about how customers are onboarded and supported here.
answerGuide: Who are your typical customers and what do they need most?
How are customers onboarded and how long does it take?
What are the most common issues or reasons customers leave?
How do you measure success for this team?
pitfalls: Questions that show you didn't read the job post.
followUps: What would you do about that?
What do you think is most important?

prompt: Is there anything else you would like us to know about you?
variants: Anything you wish I had asked?
Is there something we have not covered?
intent: Last chance to fill a gap or strengthen your close.
answerGuide: Pick the one point not yet covered that matters most to this role.
Add one line of proof.
Reaffirm interest.
followUps: What should we remember about you?

prompt: Give me your closing statement: why should we move you forward?
variants: Make your final pitch.
Sum up why you are the right fit.
intent: Tests a concise closing pitch with two strengths tied to their needs, one proof point and a clear ask.
answerGuide: Restate interest in the role.
Two strengths tied to what they said they need, with one proof point.
Ask about next steps.
followUps: What are you most sure of?

prompt: Do you have any concerns about your fit that I can address now?
variants: After talking to me, do you have hesitations about the role?
intent: Some interviewers invite you to check your own fit. Be tactful.
answerGuide: Ask what the interviewer sees as the main gap in your background.
Address it with one proof point.
Confirm your enthusiasm.
followUps: Is there anything I can clarify?

prompt: What are the next steps in the process and when can we expect to decide?
variants: Ask about timeline at the end.
intent: Practical close: ask what happens next and when, so you can follow up properly.
answerGuide: Ask what happens next and the timeline.
Ask whom to follow up with.
Thank them and send a note within a day.
followUps: Do you need anything from me?

prompt: Questions to ask about growth and development.
variants: What would you ask about career growth?
intent: Shows long-term interest without sounding entitled.
answerGuide: What does growth look like for someone who succeeds in this role?
How does the team support learning (mentoring, training, stretch work)?
Where have people in this role gone next?
pitfalls: Asking about promotion before understanding the job.
followUps: What would you want to learn?
What skills would you build first?
How do you like to be developed?

prompt: What question would you ask to learn what the interviewer likes best and finds hardest about working here?
variants: How would you ask about the company culture?
intent: A rapport question that draws out the interviewer's honest view of the best and hardest parts of the job.
answerGuide: Ask: What do you enjoy most about working here, and what is the hardest part?
Listen for specifics rather than slogans.
Follow up on anything surprising.
followUps: Does that fit what you want?

prompt: How would you follow up after the interview?
variants: Would you send a thank-you note?
intent: Tests professional follow-up: a prompt, specific note that restates fit.
answerGuide: Send a brief thank-you within a day referencing a specific topic discussed.
Restate interest and add one relevant point.
Follow up politely on the timeline given.
followUps: Who do you send it to?

prompt: Recruiter screen: what questions do you ask at the end of the call?
variants: Do you have questions about the process?
intent: Phone-screen close: logistics and role clarity questions that show you listened and help you decide.
answerGuide: Ask about the interview stages and timeline.
Ask about the salary band and work arrangements (hours, time zone, equipment).
Ask what the team looks for in the first months.
Confirm next steps and contact.

prompt: Hiring-manager round: what do you ask about how success is measured in the first 90 days?
variants: Do you have questions for me as the manager?
intent: Hiring-manager question set that signals you plan to perform and want clarity on expectations.
answerGuide: Ask what a strong first 90 days look like and which measures matter.
Ask about team priorities and biggest current problem.
Ask how the manager gives feedback and how often.
Ask what typically separates good from great.
followUps: What would you do with the answer?

prompt: Panel round: how do you tailor your questions to the different people on the panel?
variants: What do you ask a panel?
intent: Shows research and respect for each panelist's perspective.
answerGuide: Ask the engineer about release process and quality.
Ask the product person about priorities and customers.
Ask the support or success person about customer pain.
Ask everyone what they enjoy most.
pitfalls: Directing every question to the manager.
followUps: What if all questions were answered?

prompt: What questions would you ask about AI tools and team tooling?
variants: Ask us about how we work with AI.
intent: Signals modern working practice and care about data policy.
answerGuide: Ask whether there is an AI policy and which tools are approved.
Ask how the team verifies AI-assisted work.
Ask what tools the team uses for tickets, testing and documentation.
Ask about training.
followUps: What if the policy is strict?

prompt: What do you ask a remote team about how they communicate and make decisions?
variants: Questions about remote work for the interviewer.
intent: Checks that you understand the practical side of async work and want to fit it.
answerGuide: Ask how decisions are recorded and shared.
Ask about core hours, meeting load and response expectations.
Ask how new joiners are onboarded remotely.
Ask how the team handles time zones.
pitfalls: Asking whether you can work whenever.

prompt: Final round: before we finish, what concerns do you think we have about you, and how would you answer them?
variants: Is there anything about your candidacy that gives you pause?
intent: Shows self-awareness and gives a chance to deal with objections directly.
answerGuide: Name the likely concern (small-team background, limited automation depth).
Answer with evidence and a plan.
Ask whether it is a concern for them.
End on enthusiasm.

prompt: Write the first two lines of your thank-you note to a hiring manager after the interview.
variants: How would you follow up in writing?
intent: Short writing exercise: specific, quick and useful.
answerGuide: Thank them with a specific detail from the conversation.
Restate fit in one line.
Answer any question you handled loosely.
Send within a day.

prompt: You are given a take-home exercise. Which questions do you ask before you start?
variants: How do you approach assessments?
intent: Take-home etiquette: scope, time, deliverable format and evaluation criteria.
answerGuide: Ask about time expectation and deadline.
Ask about the deliverable format and the audience.
Ask what tools and data you can use and whether AI assistance is allowed.
Ask how it will be evaluated.
followUps: What if they do not answer?

prompt: Question to ask: why is this position open, and what happened to the last person in it?
variants: Is this a new role or a replacement?
How long has the position been open?
intent: A question for you to ask. The answer tells you about growth, turnover and expectations.
answerGuide: Ask it neutrally, near the end.
Listen for whether it is growth, a promotion or turnover, and for how they speak about the previous person.
Follow up on what they want done differently this time.
Use the answer to restate how you fit.
pitfalls: Asking in a tone that sounds suspicious.
followUps: What would you ask next if they say the last person left after six months?

prompt: Question to ask: what would a successful first ninety days look like in this role?
variants: What would you want me to have achieved by the end of the first quarter?
How will my performance be measured?
intent: One of the most useful questions you can ask: it shows you are thinking about results and it tells you what to prepare for.
answerGuide: Ask it of the hiring manager.
Note the specifics they give and reflect one back with relevant experience.
Ask what usually gets in the way for new people.
Use what you learn in your thank-you note.
pitfalls: Asking and then not responding to the answer.
Asking it of a recruiter who cannot know.
followUps: How would you use their answer in the rest of the interview?

prompt: Question to ask: how would you describe your management style and how the team works together day to day?
variants: How does the team communicate when remote?
How do you give feedback?
intent: A question for you to ask. For a remote role the answer tells you how you would actually spend your days.
answerGuide: Ask about meetings, written updates and how decisions are made.
Ask how feedback is given and how often.
Ask who you would work with most.
Compare the answer with how you work best.
pitfalls: Asking questions already answered in the posting.
